Keep the working envelope near 18 meters wide, 14 meters deep, and 9 meters high. Only reviewed protrusions such as signs, arms, doors, mirrors, roots, branches, railings, hoses, lighting, propulsion, awnings, stairs, or service hardware may extend beyond it. Every major and secondary form must reinforce Starter 6twelve Exterior; unrelated decorative mass should be removed.

Construction and functional anatomy: Model a coherent foundation, frame or load-bearing wall system, layered facade or structural depth, human-scale access, glazing or openings with frames, weather and drainage treatment, service access, and credible transitions between materials. Each one must connect through credible frames, joints, seams, foundations, roots, brackets, fasteners, cables, pipes, glazing frames, hinges, biological attachment, serving structure, packaging, or material transitions. Flat paint, decals, and emission may not replace a component that explains operation, weight support, access, occupancy, growth, containment, drainage, power, preparation, protection, or maintenance.

Materials, color, and lighting: use the named material vocabulary painted metal, concrete, ordinary glass, galvanized hardware, warm brick, cream, storefront blue, civic navy, school green, utility gray, residential sage. welcoming, lived-in American city realism; warm brick, stucco, concrete, patched asphalt, painted metal, ordinary civic and residential materials. Metal surfaces need distinct painted, powder-coated, galvanized, brushed, cast, polished, oxidized, or heat-affected responses rather than one universal gray material. Glass requires thickness, framing, tint appropriate to the town, controlled transparency, believable roughness, and an interior or backing surface so it does not read as an empty blue plane. Stone, brick, concrete, plaster, stucco, tile, and asphalt should show scale-correct joints, aggregate or surface breakup, edge wear, drainage staining, and construction transitions without noisy procedural speckling. Wood needs believable board direction, grain scale, end grain, joinery, sealing, wear, and moisture response appropriate to indoor, residential, marine, fantasy, or industrial use. Fabric, upholstery, leather, rubber, and flexible polymers require thickness, seams, compression or tension cues, stitching where visible, and roughness variation tied to handling. Emissive accents must arise from a lens, strip, screen, projector, fixture, biological organ, or energy component. Do not paint unexplained neon lines across ordinary structure. Avoid the town-specific failures: citywide neon wash, toy-town proportions, sterile empty streets. Surface variation should follow manufacturing, age, handling, weather, moisture, heat, pressure, preparation, cleaning, or maintenance rather than random noise. Emissive areas must originate from a real lens, screen, fixture, projector, biological organ, or energy system.

Condition and environmental integration: Apply restrained lived-in wear at contact points, lower edges, hinges, handles, feet, fasteners, drainage paths, service openings, tires, exposed corners, or frequently cleaned surfaces. Match the district’s maintenance level rather than using uniform dirt or uniform perfection. Place it on the parcel, terrain shelf, dock edge, modular foundation, or interior footprint named by the blueprint. Public access faces navigation and social space; service access faces the alley, utility corridor, backstage zone, waterfront service edge, or maintenance route. Foundation, stairs, ramps, porches, piles, retaining walls, and terrain transitions must meet the environment without floating gaps. Add contact shadows, foundations, feet, brackets, roots, piles, seals, trim, drainage, terrain blending, waterline response, or wall transitions where the object meets its environment. It may not appear pasted into the scene or suspended by invisible support unless the design explicitly includes a justified force, mount, cable, lift field, or suspension system.

Interaction and state design: Keep entrances, shutters, gates, windows, awnings, stairs, ramps, elevators, signs, lighting, roof equipment, and service components separable whenever gameplay or state changes may need them. Expected hooks include transform, material-state, damage, pickup, or placement hook only where gameplay requires it. Separate and name parts that can open, slide, rotate, illuminate, display content, receive an item, carry an occupant, change material, emit particles, take damage, be repaired, be harvested, or connect to another system. Static detail should remain efficient, but useful gameplay state boundaries may not be merged away.

Collision, orientation, and export: Use modular floor, wall, roof, stair, rail, counter, doorway, foundation, and major structural collision. Walkable areas, entrances, windows used for gameplay, and service openings must match the visible model, while trim, roof equipment, cables, fasteners, and inaccessible facade detail remain simplified or nonblocking. Use positive Z as the principal entrance, public face, or module-forward direction and positive Y as up after export conversion. Place the origin at ground level or the documented connection plane near the footprint center. Use one named asset root, semantically named render meshes, separate animated or stateful parts, simplified collision, and metadata for asset ID, town, family, source document, license, dimensions, final semantic category, and specification version. Remove preview cameras, lights, helpers, unused materials, duplicates, hidden placeholders, and accidental geometry before GLB export.

Performance and LOD: Preserve massing, entrances, openings, supports, and skyline in every LOD. Repeating windows, panels, rails, trim, and structural members should use shared geometry or instancing. Close-range output may use up to the reviewed maximum, with a practical target near 39,000 triangles when silhouette and required components justify it. Medium-range output should target roughly 18,000 triangles while preserving primary form, supports, interaction components, openings, material blocks, and essential lights. Far output should target roughly 6,000 triangles or a suitable impostor while retaining the recognizable outline, mounting or ground relationship, and major color or emissive signature. Reduction may never destroy this recognition requirement: Establish the building or structural-module category from massing, roof or overhead profile, entrance or connection hierarchy, structural bays, openings, and ground or support relationship before signage and color are visible.

Acceptance standard: the final model must look intentional from every inspection angle, satisfy every required component, fit the reviewed scale, use meaningful material separation, remain inside geometry budgets, sit correctly on its placement plane, and export as a verified nonempty GLB. A technically valid file that looks generic, toy-like, structurally impossible, context-free, semantically misclassified, or unlike Starter 6twelve Exterior is a failure. Correct it, retry it, or quarantine it instead of publishing it.

It originates from docs/STARTER_TOWN_BLUEPRINT.md under “A. Functional building exteriors.” A production-ready Starter Block Supply Exterior, designed as a architectural exterior shell for Starter Town. Use believable structural bays, facade depth, doors at human scale, roof drainage or parapet logic, service access, and a recognizable public-facing silhouette. The object must remain immediately recognizable from silhouette and required components, use physically coherent construction and human or vehicle scale, and follow the town direction: welcoming, lived-in American city realism; warm brick, stucco, concrete, patched asphalt, painted metal, ordinary civic and residential materials. This asset appears under the blueprint section “A. Functional building exteriors” and should visibly support that gameplay or environmental role rather than acting as generic filler. The blueprint evidence is: Willowbend residents leave for school/work in the morning. Scholar's Quarter gets students and buses during school hours. Northworks peaks during daytime shifts. Dreamdrop District peaks midday and evening. WorkTower peaks morning and late afternoon. Parkside peaks afternoon/evening. Eastgate has continuous traveler traffic. NPCs should not all walk one square loop. Pedestrian routes must be district-specific and connected by selected cross-town paths. --- 20. Transportation and map UI Player transportation walking/running owned/stolen cars future bus/fast travel cross-town driving remains the primary Starter Town experience Transit nodes No new enterable transit building is required. Use: bus shelters at Dreamdrop, Zaylins Prep, WorkTower, Parkside, and Eastgate Eastgate fast-travel marker later North Gate highway marker Minimap requirements dynamic bounds for 500x480 city district labels roads visible by hierarchy player home marker school, job board, police, fuel, garage, shops, park active mission route wanted-search area later World map requirement Starter Town should appear as a real city silhouette with recognizable district shapes, not a square icon. --- 21. Asset families A. Functional building exteriors

Physical identity and semantic decision: the final category is architecture because strong filename prefix resolves the physical object as architecture. Model it as a complete architectural asset with a legible public face, believable side and service elevations, and construction logic appropriate to its use. Words describing an animal, profession, customer, owner, district, collection, or story function may not force character or creature anatomy onto an object such as a cottage, boat, crate, display, station, rack, board, feeder, machine, sign, or piece of equipment. The named object must be identifiable in neutral clay material before labels, color, and glow are applied.

Silhouette and proportion: Establish the building or structural-module category from massing, roof or overhead profile, entrance or connection hierarchy, structural bays, openings, and ground or support relationship before signage and color are visible. Keep the working envelope near 18 meters wide, 14 meters deep, and 9 meters high. Only reviewed protrusions such as signs, arms, doors, mirrors, roots, branches, railings, hoses, lighting, propulsion, awnings, stairs, or service hardware may extend beyond it. Every major and secondary form must reinforce Starter Block Supply Exterior; unrelated decorative mass should be removed.

Construction and functional anatomy: Model a coherent foundation, frame or load-bearing wall system, layered facade or structural depth, human-scale access, glazing or openings with frames, weather and drainage treatment, service access, and credible transitions between materials. Required visible components are primary massing, roof line, entrance, window system, facade material breaks, service side, foundation. Each one must connect through credible frames, joints, seams, foundations, roots, brackets, fasteners, cables, pipes, glazing frames, hinges, biological attachment, serving structure, packaging, or material transitions. Flat paint, decals, and emission may not replace a component that explains operation, weight support, access, occupancy, growth, containment, drainage, power, preparation, protection, or maintenance.

Materials, color, and lighting: use the named material vocabulary painted metal, concrete, ordinary glass, galvanized hardware, warm brick, cream, storefront blue, civic navy, school green, utility gray, residential sage. welcoming, lived-in American city realism; warm brick, stucco, concrete, patched asphalt, painted metal, ordinary civic and residential materials. Metal surfaces need distinct painted, powder-coated, galvanized, brushed, cast, polished, oxidized, or heat-affected responses rather than one universal gray material. Glass requires thickness, framing, tint appropriate to the town, controlled transparency, believable roughness, and an interior or backing surface so it does not read as an empty blue plane. Stone, brick, concrete, plaster, stucco, tile, and asphalt should show scale-correct joints, aggregate or surface breakup, edge wear, drainage staining, and construction transitions without noisy procedural speckling. Wood needs believable board direction, grain scale, end grain, joinery, sealing, wear, and moisture response appropriate to indoor, residential, marine, fantasy, or industrial use. Fabric, upholstery, leather, rubber, and flexible polymers require thickness, seams, compression or tension cues, stitching where visible, and roughness variation tied to handling. Emissive accents must arise from a lens, strip, screen, projector, fixture, biological organ, or energy component. Do not paint unexplained neon lines across ordinary structure. Avoid the town-specific failures: citywide neon wash, toy-town proportions, sterile empty streets. Surface variation should follow manufacturing, age, handling, weather, moisture, heat, pressure, preparation, cleaning, or maintenance rather than random noise. Emissive areas must originate from a real lens, screen, fixture, projector, biological organ, or energy system.

Condition and environmental integration: Apply restrained lived-in wear at contact points, lower edges, hinges, handles, feet, fasteners, drainage paths, service openings, tires, exposed corners, or frequently cleaned surfaces. Match the district’s maintenance level rather than using uniform dirt or uniform perfection. Place it on the parcel, terrain shelf, dock edge, modular foundation, or interior footprint named by the blueprint. Public access faces navigation and social space; service access faces the alley, utility corridor, backstage zone, waterfront service edge, or maintenance route. Foundation, stairs, ramps, porches, piles, retaining walls, and terrain transitions must meet the environment without floating gaps. Add contact shadows, foundations, feet, brackets, roots, piles, seals, trim, drainage, terrain blending, waterline response, or wall transitions where the object meets its environment. It may not appear pasted into the scene or suspended by invisible support unless the design explicitly includes a justified force, mount, cable, lift field, or suspension system.

Interaction and state design: Keep entrances, shutters, gates, windows, awnings, stairs, ramps, elevators, signs, lighting, roof equipment, and service components separable whenever gameplay or state changes may need them. Expected hooks include transform, material-state, damage, pickup, or placement hook only where gameplay requires it. Separate and name parts that can open, slide, rotate, illuminate, display content, receive an item, carry an occupant, change material, emit particles, take damage, be repaired, be harvested, or connect to another system. Static detail should remain efficient, but useful gameplay state boundaries may not be merged away.

Collision, orientation, and export: Use modular floor, wall, roof, stair, rail, counter, doorway, foundation, and major structural collision. Walkable areas, entrances, windows used for gameplay, and service openings must match the visible model, while trim, roof equipment, cables, fasteners, and inaccessible facade detail remain simplified or nonblocking. Use positive Z as the principal entrance, public face, or module-forward direction and positive Y as up after export conversion. Place the origin at ground level or the documented connection plane near the footprint center. Use one named asset root, semantically named render meshes, separate animated or stateful parts, simplified collision, and metadata for asset ID, town, family, source document, license, dimensions, final semantic category, and specification version. Remove preview cameras, lights, helpers, unused materials, duplicates, hidden placeholders, and accidental geometry before GLB export.

Performance and LOD: Preserve massing, entrances, openings, supports, and skyline in every LOD. Repeating windows, panels, rails, trim, and structural members should use shared geometry or instancing. Close-range output may use up to the reviewed maximum, with a practical target near 39,000 triangles when silhouette and required components justify it. Medium-range output should target roughly 18,000 triangles while preserving primary form, supports, interaction components, openings, material blocks, and essential lights. Far output should target roughly 6,000 triangles or a suitable impostor while retaining the recognizable outline, mounting or ground relationship, and major color or emissive signature. Reduction may never destroy this recognition requirement: Establish the building or structural-module category from massing, roof or overhead profile, entrance or connection hierarchy, structural bays, openings, and ground or support relationship before signage and color are visible.

Acceptance standard: the final model must look intentional from every inspection angle, satisfy every required component, fit the reviewed scale, use meaningful material separation, remain inside geometry budgets, sit correctly on its placement plane, and export as a verified nonempty GLB. A technically valid file that looks generic, toy-like, structurally impossible, context-free, semantically misclassified, or unlike Starter Block Supply Exterior is a failure. Correct it, retry it, or quarantine it instead of publishing it.

materialPlan.metalRule: Metal surfaces need distinct painted, powder-coated, galvanized, brushed, cast, polished, oxidized, or heat-affected responses rather than one universal gray material.

materialPlan.masonryRule: Stone, brick, concrete, plaster, stucco, tile, and asphalt should show scale-correct joints, aggregate or surface breakup, edge wear, drainage staining, and construction transitions without noisy procedural speckling.
materialPlan.woodRule: Wood needs believable board direction, grain scale, end grain, joinery, sealing, wear, and moisture response appropriate to indoor, residential, marine, fantasy, or industrial use.
materialPlan.flexibleRule: Fabric, upholstery, leather, rubber, and flexible polymers require thickness, seams, compression or tension cues, stitching where visible, and roughness variation tied to handling.

Starter Town community Mildew Patch Standard is a procedural-decal added by the final Zaylins gameplay, sensory, environmental, interaction, customization, and cohesion sweep for starter-town. It closes the “community decal” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following contemporary neighborhood and civic design with warm practical materials, family-friendly clarity, and believable everyday wear.

Required production anatomy: projection boundary, primary mark silhouette, secondary edge breakup, opacity mask, surface normal response, scale variation, fade lifecycle, clean or child-safe alternative. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Starter Town community Mildew Patch Standard. Materials and response layers include vector color layer, opacity mask, roughness response, normal or height suggestion. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Starter Town community Mildew Patch Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Specialized GLBs remain outside the generic primitive Blender lane until a dedicated builder can satisfy this contract.

Starter Town delivery Card Reader Standard is a dedicated-prop-builder added by the final Zaylins gameplay, sensory, environmental, interaction, customization, and cohesion sweep for starter-town. It closes the “delivery infrastructure” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following contemporary neighborhood and civic design with warm practical materials, family-friendly clarity, and believable everyday wear.

Required production anatomy: anchored base or mount, structural enclosure or frame, primary operating surface, user control or connection, service access, power, conduit, drainage, or network path, safety and weather protection, fasteners and identification. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Starter Town delivery Card Reader Standard. Materials and response layers include painted or galvanized structure, service hardware, control or lens material, foundation or mounting material. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Starter Town delivery Card Reader Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following contemporary neighborhood and civic design with warm practical materials, family-friendly clarity, and believable everyday wear.

Required production anatomy: anchored base or mount, structural enclosure or frame, primary operating surface, user control or connection, service access, power, conduit, drainage, or network path, safety and weather protection, fasteners and identification. Every component is functional. Materials and response layers include painted or galvanized structure, service hardware, control or lens material, foundation or mounting material. It closes the “playground decal” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following contemporary neighborhood and civic design with warm practical materials, family-friendly clarity, and believable everyday wear.

Required production anatomy: projection boundary, primary mark silhouette, secondary edge breakup, opacity mask, surface normal response, scale variation, fade lifecycle, clean or child-safe alternative. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Starter Town playground Barnacle Patch Standard. Materials and response layers include vector color layer, opacity mask, roughness response, normal or height suggestion. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Starter Town playground Barnacle Patch Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Specialized GLBs remain outside the generic primitive Blender lane until a dedicated builder can satisfy this contract.

assets.description:
Starter Town retail Water Caustic Projection Standard is a procedural-runtime-effect added by the final Zaylins gameplay, sensory, environmental, interaction, customization, and cohesion sweep for starter-town. It closes the “retail runtime-vfx” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following contemporary neighborhood and civic design with warm practical materials, family-friendly clarity, and believable everyday wear.

Required production anatomy: named emitter origin, primary particle or optical layer, secondary breakup layer, timing envelope, surface or volume response, quality tiers, pooling and cleanup rule, reduced-motion and reduced-flash alternative. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Starter Town retail Water Caustic Projection Standard. Materials and response layers include particle sprite or procedural field, optical or emissive layer, surface-response mask, accessibility fallback. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Starter Town retail Water Caustic Projection Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Specialized GLBs remain outside the generic primitive Blender lane until a dedicated builder can satisfy this contract.

Starter Town school Fire Alarm Pull Standard is a dedicated-prop-builder added by the final Zaylins gameplay, sensory, environmental, interaction, customization, and cohesion sweep for starter-town. It closes the “school infrastructure” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following contemporary neighborhood and civic design with warm practical materials, family-friendly clarity, and believable everyday wear.

Required production anatomy: anchored base or mount, structural enclosure or frame, primary operating surface, user control or connection, service access, power, conduit, drainage, or network path, safety and weather protection, fasteners and identification. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Starter Town school Fire Alarm Pull Standard. Materials and response layers include painted or galvanized structure, service hardware, control or lens material, foundation or mounting material. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Starter Town school Fire Alarm Pull Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Specialized GLBs remain outside the generic primitive Blender lane until a dedicated builder can satisfy this contract.

Starter Town school Pressure Equalizer Standard is a dedicated-prop-builder added by the final Zaylins gameplay, sensory, environmental, interaction, customization, and cohesion sweep for starter-town. It closes the “school infrastructure” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following contemporary neighborhood and civic design with warm practical materials, family-friendly clarity, and believable everyday wear.

Required production anatomy: anchored base or mount, structural enclosure or frame, primary operating surface, user control or connection, service access, power, conduit, drainage, or network path, safety and weather protection, fasteners and identification. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Starter Town school Pressure Equalizer Standard. Materials and response layers include painted or galvanized structure, service hardware, control or lens material, foundation or mounting material. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Starter Town school Pressure Equalizer Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Specialized GLBs remain outside the generic primitive Blender lane until a dedicated builder can satisfy this contract.

It closes the “school connector” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following contemporary neighborhood and civic design with warm practical materials, family-friendly clarity, and believable everyday wear.

Required production anatomy: primary structural span, start connection socket, end connection socket, load-bearing frame, service access, seal or transition trim, collision-safe boundary, LOD-preserved silhouette. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Starter Town school Transit Tube Merge Standard. Materials and response layers include structural material, connection hardware, seal or trim material, town-specific surface finish. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Starter Town school Transit Tube Merge Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Specialized GLBs remain outside the generic primitive Blender lane until a dedicated builder can satisfy this contract.
